Q: Cosmos DB data migration A:

I encountered the same requirement and developed a C# application that can address this use case. It allows you to copy all items from one container to another within the same Cosmos DB account, to a different Cosmos DB account using the same connection string, or even to a Cosmos DB instance using a completely separate connection. Feel free to test it and let me know whether it meets your needs.

Q: Line does not start with any known Prisma schema keyword error on Python A:

Just i case someone finds this thread looking for an answer but (for me) different problem triggered the error:

enum EnumName
{
    Prop1
    Prop2
}

This is not accepted, throws the error. The "{" symbol needs to be in the same line as the "enum" keyword.

enum EnumName {
    Prop1
    Prop2
}

As far as i know, this is NOT present in the Prisma documentation, but please correct me if i am wrong.

Q: Error when linking files in big-endian mode : libgcc_s.so.1: error adding symbols: file in wrong format A:

The error occurs because your big-endian object files are being linked against the system's little-endian libgcc_s.so.1, which are incompatible formats

Since you're writing pure assembly, you don't need C runtime at all, just add -nostdlib

arm-linux-gnueabi -o memory memory.o io.o -mbig-endian -z noexecstack -nostdlib

If you ever do need full library support, you'd need a proper big-endian toolchain (arm-linux-gnueabibe) instead, since arm-linux-gnueabi is little-endian by default and its prebuild libraries reflect that

Also note: your compile commands show arm-linux-gnueabi instead of arm-linux-gnueabi-gcc , likely just a typo in the post
